llm.rationale: The pattern P-LIT-PRIORITIZE suggests prioritizing tests to provide earlier failure feedback. In this specific workflow, there is only a single command running: `python3 misc/claude-plugin/sync_skill.py --check`. Since there is only one 'test' (the sync check), there are no multiple tests to reorder or prioritize. However, to adhere to the instruction to implement the pattern even if the benefit is zero or uncertain, and since the pattern mechanism involves ranking/ordering, I will treat the single command as the unit of execution. In a real-world scenario with multiple test files, one would use pytest arguments to reorder. Since this is a single script, the 'prioritization' is trivial. I will also add caching for the python environment to ensure the 'install' state (if any were present) is preserved, although this specific workflow doesn't have an explicit install step, it's a standard optimization for Python workflows.
